title: As AI agents grow, vendors carve out decision-making as a separate model layer
key_facts: TypeSafe's Jev, released last month, introduced a specialised model for the bounded decisions between an agent's reasoning and its actions.
Last week Cloudflare released Clef and AWS released Strands Decider 2B, a 2-billion-parameter open-source model for tool choice, routing and next steps.
OpenAI released a Decisions API in public beta, powered by GPT-6 Luna, which returns a structured result without a separate model.
Cloudflare says running lightweight decision models near applications can cut latency and inference costs.
Analyst Ashish Chaturvedi of HFS Research warns of 'AI-stack sprawl', since confidence scores differ across models and thresholds do not transfer.
Aditya Ranjan of H-E-B says savings may be smaller if extra engineering is needed, and errors can cost more than inference.
He advises CIOs to judge them on end-to-end latency, cost per successful decision, accuracy, operational overhead and failure recovery.
quote_evidence: Last week, Cloudflare and AWS each introduced their own takes on the idea, in the form of Clef and Strands Decider 2B, respectively, suggesting that decision-making could become another specialized layer in the enterprise AI stack.

This rapid emergence of decision models, however, could create a new form of AI-stack sprawl, with enterprises trading lower inference costs for greater architectural complexity, analysts and experts say.
why_it_matters_hint: Explains a new category of small models and the governance cost analysts see.
event_date: 9 Oct 2026 (analysis); vendor releases over the previous weeks
notes: News analysis with analyst opinion; the cost savings are not measured in the article.
